description: §61.2 — a `path=` whose value is not a string literal is E-ENDPOINT-PATH-MISSING even when the attribute reader only warns about the value (`path=(x is some)` — W-IS-SOME-DEPRECATED). The bootstrap compiled it with no error and mounted no route until the S480 #2012 review (F1): a Warning inside the attribute suppressed the attribute's own code.
provenance: review:#2012-S239 F1; the §61.2 rule ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S480-four-recs-2 item 1 (PA ruling S480, #1998 review r2 N1)
rationale: §61.2: "a `path=` / `method=` / `accepts=` / `cors=` written with no value, or with a value that is not its production's form, is that attribute's code" — `path-attr ::= 'path=' string-literal`.
